text.p: Acer Computer International Ltd said on Tuesday it expected better financial results in 1997.
"I believe 1997 will be a better year for ACI (Acer Computer International). We are doing a lot of good things and right things," said William Lu, chief executive officer of Acer Computer.
He added that Acer expected its profits to grow faster in 1997 than the 4.7 percent seen in 1996.
He said Acer's strategy for 1997 was to bring "fresh technology" to the market faster than its competitors.
This would help it achieve better margins, he said.
The company would also maintain tight inventory control.
He said Acer was aiming to maintain a 10-day inventory period for price-sensitive components like Dynamic Random Access Memories (DRAMs) and central processing units (CPUs).
Lu said profit growth dropped in 1996 due mainly to the fall in DRAM prices and poor performance in certain subsidiaries, particularly in Russia and Australia.
He said server sales contracted in 1996 because the company's attention was diverted to its Acer Aspire products.
He expected server sales to grow in 1997.

He said that Acer's low-price personal computers -- Acer Basic -- did not perform as well as expected in 1996 because it was based on 486 technology. He said the company had relaunched Acer Basic using faster Pentium 120 Mhz and 136 Mhz CPUs.
He said the relaunched Acer Basic was being priced a little higher but was still below US$1,000. It was targeted mainly at developing countries, such as Indonesia, India and China.
Lu said the personal computer industry should grow at an average 15 percent per year for the next 10 years but said it was difficult to predict where DRAM prices would go.
He added that Acer's tight inventory control would help it cushion some of the price volatility.
